title: Changes in spleen size in acute sepsis and acute thrombotic events – a retrospective CT-based volume analysis for the clinical translation of experimental findings
summary: In cases of severe infections or acute blood clots, the size of the spleen may change because it may play a role in regulating blood platelets. It is not yet known whether this actually occurs in humans. This study investigates whether spleen size changes in people with acute sepsis or an acute thrombotic event compared to a healthy baseline. To this end, previous CT scans from three small groups of patients will be analyzed. Spleen volume will be measured and compared between the two time points. No additional examinations will be conducted, as only existing data will be used.
conditions: Sepsis A41.9, thrombosis I80, and healthy controls

interventions.name: Patients are identified retrospectively via PACS/RIS. Three groups (sepsis, thrombotic event, controls), each consisting of 10 individuals, are randomly selected. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
belong to one of the three defined groups:
acute sepsis
acute thrombotic event
Control group without an acute event

Have two CT scans:
one CT scan during the acute clinical phase (≤ 48 hours after the event)
one comparison CT scan without acute illness

Be documented in the PACS/RIS of LMU Medical Center between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025
Exclusion criteria:
Missing one of the two CT scans (acute or follow-up CT)

No acute event (for sepsis or thrombosis group)

No suitable control group

Time period outside 2010–2025

Incomplete or uninterpretable CT data
